title: Spatial relationships and cultivation of the microbiome
summary: The human gut is home to billions of microorganisms that influence our health. This study uses stool samples from 10 healthy volunteers to develop two methods: First, to visualize which microbes live next to each other in the gut. Second, to grow gut microbes in the lab alongside intestinal cells to study how they interact.

interventions.name: Stool samples from healthy volunteers (n=10) will be used to (1) visualize the spatial arrangement of microbial species via CLASI-FISH and (2) transfer stool-derived microbial consortia into a co-culture system with intestinal epithelial cells to perform functional assays.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Capable of giving informed consent, voluntary participant
Exclusion criteria:
Heart failure NYHA class I–IV
Renal insufficiency stage 1–5
Hepatic insufficiency Child-Pugh A/B/C
Presence of severe rheumatic disease
Presence of severe autoimmune disease
Antibiotic use within the last 4 weeks
Malignant disease within the last ten years
Pregnancy
